newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: S.AFRICAN STOCK MARKET CLOSING REPORT.
newsitem.headline: S.AFRICAN STOCK MARKET CLOSING REPORT.

text.p: South African all share index climbed to a fresh high at the close of a mixed trading day on Tuesday, dealers said.
The index rose 30.1 points to 7,203.2 against a backdrop of a stronger rand and generally upbeat sentiment, dealers said.

"The market has actually been very firm across the board. The weaker rand this afternoon has helped the rand gold price and this has led to a bit of a demand for most of our gold stocks," one dealer said.
The rand extended its Monday rally to firm a further two cents on Tuesday, bringing its gains to almost eight cents so far this week.
Golds moved higher on the back of a steady bullion price, dealers said. The index finished 9.2 points up at 1,538.5.

"The gold price is moving better constantly at $353. I think a lot of American players have been hedging against the Dow on the gold price and I think this is going to push it better," one dealer commented.
Industrials, which at the start of trade looked bullish, were tamed towards the close by losses in industrial heavyweights Barlow Rand and Sasol , they added.
However, no accurate indication could be gleaned from Johannesburg Stock Exchange figures because of an error in calculating the index, the exchange said.
An exchange official the miscalculation of the industrial index was a result of a share split over the weekend in Bearing Man , which exchange computers had failed to pick up.
The problem was expected to be rectified by Wednesday morning.
Dealers said, however, that disappointment in Sasol's interim results had put a damper on the industrial market.

The counter shed 250 cents to 51.50 after reporting earnings of 207.7 cents per share in the year to December 25 from 174.1 cents in the previous year. Dealers said the results were below market expectations.
Barlow Rand shed 125 cents to 48.75 rand.
"The industrials were a bit overpriced in the morning. They are now consolidating before making a new upward effort," one dealer commented.

Mining house Gencor was also actively traded ahead of its results at 1400 GMT. It's share rose 45 cents to 19.95 rand before it reported earnings of 60.2 cents per share in the six months to December 31 from 50.5 cents in the 1995 period.
Overall trading volumes on the day were pegged at around 944 million rand.
